item.vignette: A patient with plaque psoriasis receives a selective TYK2 inhibitor. In cell assays, receptor-mediated TYK2 activation falls even though the drug does not compete at the catalytic ATP-binding site.
item.lead_in: Which molecular interaction most directly explains this selectivity?

options.A: Binding to the TYK2 regulatory domain and stabilizing an inhibitory regulatory-catalytic interaction
options.B: Covalent binding to the JAK1 catalytic cysteine
options.C: Competitive occupation of the shared ATP-binding pocket of all JAK kinases
options.D: Degradation of TYK2 mRNA through RNA interference

item.tested_construct: Allosteric inhibition by binding the TYK2 regulatory domain
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Deucravacitinib binds the regulatory domain of TYK2 and stabilizes an inhibitory interaction between its regulatory and catalytic domains. This produces allosteric inhibition of receptor-mediated TYK2 activation and downstream STAT signaling.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. Deucravacitinib binds the TYK2 regulatory domain and allosterically suppresses catalytic activation.
distractor_explanations.B: It does not act by covalently targeting JAK1.
distractor_explanations.C: Its selectivity is not produced by competitive occupancy of the conserved catalytic ATP site.
distractor_explanations.D: Deucravacitinib is not an RNA-interference therapy.
distractor_explanations.E: STAT signaling decreases downstream, but STAT DNA-binding domains are not the direct drug target.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish regulatory-domain allosteric TYK2 inhibition from catalytic-site JAK inhibition and downstream STAT blockade.

item.vignette: A patient with primary biliary cholangitis receives elafibranor. Activation of PPAR signaling increases FGF21-dependent suppression of a hepatic enzyme that catalyzes the rate-limiting step in conversion of cholesterol to bile acids.
item.lead_in: Which enzyme is most directly downregulated in this pathway?
item.tested_construct: PPAR-linked FGF21-dependent downregulation of CYP7A1 and reduced bile acid synthesis
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Elafibranor and its active metabolite are PPAR agonists. A label-described pathway potentially relevant to therapeutic effect involves PPAR-delta signaling, FGF21, and downregulation of CYP7A1, the key enzyme in bile acid synthesis from cholesterol.

distractor_explanations.A: HMG-CoA reductase controls cholesterol synthesis rather than the key bile-acid synthetic step described here.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. CYP7A1 is the key enzyme in bile acid synthesis from cholesterol and is downregulated in the described pathway.
distractor_explanations.C: CYP27A1 participates in an alternative bile acid pathway but is not the enzyme specified in this signaling sequence.
distractor_explanations.D: ACAT esterifies cholesterol and is not the direct downstream enzyme described.
distractor_explanations.E: Squalene epoxidase participates in cholesterol synthesis and is not the target of this pathway.

explanation.educational_objective: Link PPAR/FGF21 signaling with CYP7A1 downregulation and reduced hepatic bile acid synthesis.

item.vignette: A patient with IgA nephropathy receives a single oral agent that reduces signaling from both endothelin-1 and angiotensin II while sparing endothelin type B and angiotensin II type 2 receptors.
item.lead_in: Which receptor pair is directly antagonized?
item.tested_construct: Dual antagonism of endothelin type A and angiotensin II type 1 receptors
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Sparsentan is a single molecule with high-affinity antagonism of the endothelin type A receptor (ETA) and angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1), with much greater selectivity over ETB and AT2 receptors.

distractor_explanations.A: Both listed receptors are relatively spared by sparsentan.
distractor_explanations.B: AT2 is not the angiotensin receptor directly antagonized.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. The direct target pair is ETA and AT1.
distractor_explanations.D: ETB is relatively spared; the endothelin target is ETA.
distractor_explanations.E: Beta-1 adrenergic receptors are not direct sparsentan targets.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize combined ETA and AT1 receptor antagonism as the defining dual mechanism of sparsentan.

item.vignette: A patient with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria has persistent C3-fragment opsonization of red cells despite terminal complement blockade. Danicopan is added and alternative-pathway amplification falls.
item.lead_in: Which complement protein is directly inhibited?
item.tested_construct: Reversible inhibition of complement Factor D in the alternative pathway
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Danicopan binds reversibly to complement Factor D and selectively inhibits the alternative complement pathway. This prevents Factor D-dependent cleavage of Factor B into Ba and Bb, reducing formation of the C3bBb alternative-pathway C3 convertase and downstream C3-fragment opsonization.

distractor_explanations.A: C3 is a downstream substrate and is not the direct molecular target.
distractor_explanations.B: Factor B cleavage is prevented downstream of Factor D inhibition, but Factor B is not directly bound by danicopan.
distractor_explanations.C: Properdin stabilizes the alternative-pathway C3 convertase but is not directly inhibited.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. Danicopan directly binds and inhibits Factor D.
distractor_explanations.E: C5 blockade controls the terminal pathway, whereas danicopan acts proximally in the alternative pathway.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate proximal Factor D inhibition from direct C3, Factor B, properdin, and C5 blockade in complement biology.

item.vignette: A patient with lupus nephritis receives voclosporin. T-cell cytokine production decreases after a calcium-dependent phosphatase pathway is suppressed.
item.lead_in: Which transcription factor remains relatively phosphorylated and therefore less able to activate T-cell gene expression?
item.tested_construct: Calcineurin inhibition prevents NFAT dephosphorylation and activation
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Voclosporin is a calcineurin-inhibitor immunosuppressant. Activated calcineurin normally dephosphorylates nuclear factor of activated T-cell cytoplasmic (NFATc), promoting its transcriptional activity; calcineurin inhibition therefore suppresses lymphocyte proliferation and T-cell cytokine production.

distractor_explanations.A: NF-kappaB is an inflammatory transcription factor but is not the direct calcineurin substrate described here.
distractor_explanations.B: STAT3 is activated primarily by JAK-mediated phosphorylation rather than calcineurin-dependent dephosphorylation.
distractor_explanations.C: AP-1 participates in T-cell activation but is not the phosphatase target in this mechanism.
distractor_explanations.D: CREB is regulated through kinase signaling and is not the relevant calcineurin substrate.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. Calcineurin inhibition prevents NFAT dephosphorylation and activation.

explanation.educational_objective: Link calcineurin inhibition with reduced NFAT activation and decreased T-cell cytokine transcription.
